about: The variables this skill expects the FIRMWARE to declare. One file, because these names used
to be hard-coded in twelve places and had already drifted: FrozenValue was 'true' in
live_read and '1' in read_dma, and the heartbeat candidates differed in set AND order
across four files. tools/audit_fw_contract.ps1 fails the build when any script disagrees
with this file, so the drift cannot come back.
These are the ONLY firmware symbols this skill knows by name. Everything else about the
target (memory map, Flash base, section layout, probe model) is discovered, never assumed.

identity.why: A firmware-declared build identity is compared with the value recorded at load. This detects mismatches only if each build has a unique ID; a repeated or stale ID cannot prove a SHA256 match by itself.
identity.firmware: volatile unsigned long gFwId = FW_ID;  /* generate a unique ID for every build; never reuse */

ramProof.why: When present, the RAM updater, counter and pinned map give source-location evidence without reading PC. Missing or nonadvancing evidence is reported as metadata, never a load or read veto.
ramProof.firmware: See references/ram-proof-firmware.md for an optional C and linker integration pattern.
ramProof.integration: Place the function in a section whose RUN address is RAM according to the selected .cmd/.map, call it every 1-10 ms from the running application, keep the counter in RAM, and ensure no other code writes the counter. Compiler and linker syntax are checked against the selected project before adding it.

heartbeat.why: Any ONE advancing proves the program is executing. More than one is better: gMsTick advancing while usMainLoop is frozen means interrupts still run but the main loop is stuck.
heartbeat.firmware: volatile unsigned long gMsTick;   /* ++ inside the 1 ms timer ISR */
heartbeat.firmwareExtra: volatile unsigned long usMainLoop; /* ++ inside the background for(;;) */

rate.why: Increasing only says the counter moved once. The rate says it moves at the frequency the firmware claims, which separates a live program from a value that happens to change.

frozenBuffer.why: Continuous capture is the only waveform read path: the control ISR appends one sample set per tick into a static array, sets the frozen flag when full, then stops writing. The host reads a static array, so transfer time never corrupts it. DMA ping-pong and bank selection were removed on 2026-11-18.
frozenBuffer.note: Needs exactly three symbols: one static array (in a named RAM section), one completed/frozen flag (set to 1 only after the last point is written), and one point counter or sequence number. Size the array as f_ctrl * T * V first; anything above 4096 words needs the RAMGS blocks merged into a single MEMORY entry.

readGate.why: These operational checks determine whether any current data can be read. They do not judge the captured numbers.

dataVerdict.why: When a target answers, deliver the captured values and mark the verdict FAIL if any identity, freshness, liveness or numeric check fails.

sourceMetadata.why: Report RAM, Flash or UNKNOWN with evidence; location alone cannot reject a download or suppress captured data.

timing.why: Limit program loads and repeated JTAG requests. The load gap covers retries, failed attempts and successive continuous-mode rounds; the read gap applies before each new data request.
